subject: Novasys — DPA redlines, SCCs & order form tie-ins
messages:
From: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@novasys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novasys.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass attached

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching Novasys' third pass on the DPA (tracked changes) and the transfer addendum that calls out SCCs + jurisdictional carveouts. Main asks from our side:

- Confirmation of processor vs controller roles for the features below (batching/cache, embeddings storage, and telemetry logs). We surfaced some internal ambiguity in Section 2 of the DPA.
- Clarify whether Redwood's Dedicated offering (reserved pools) changes any of the transfer controls we should expect to see in the Order Form.
- KMS/HSM options: we annotated a clause requesting HSM-backed key control for EU regulated data — need confirmation of supported integrations and any extra implementation timeline.

We'd like a proposed timeline to get to an executed DPA so procurement can align the order form SOW. Can you loop in the person who will own technical evidence (SCCs implementation notes, subprocessor list snapshot)?

Attachments: Novasys_DPA_v3_redline.docx; Transfer_Addendum_SCCs_v1.pdf

Best,
Sara
Legal Ops — Novasys Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@novasys.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass attached

Sara — thanks for the redline. Quick read-through of the three points you listed below; attaching a short comment summary and a proposed role matrix for the items you flagged.

- Roles: For the generation APIs and embeddings storage, Redwood operates as processor. We will, however, retain limited telemetry (errors, token-level latency metrics) as controller for service improvement; that telemetry will be pseudonymized per our policy. In the DPA we've proposed a carveout paragraph that keeps customer content under their control while allowing aggregated telemetry.

- Dedicated capacity: The Dedicated offering does not change transfer controls by default. Customers can opt for VPC-only deployments (Private) or region-pin in Dedicated which materially reduces cross-border transfer surfaces. We'll mark the Order Form to surface the chosen hosting mode and the related SCCs profile.

- KMS/HSM: We support cloud KMS integrated with customer-managed keys in GCP/Azure, and a bring-your-own-HSM option for Private deployments. That require a separate integration checklist (approx 3-4 weeks for standard provision + audit).

Next steps we propose:
1) Laura help finalize the delegation language (controller/processor + telemetry carveouts).
2) Ben to confirm operational evidence (subprocessor list snapshot, SOC2 pointers, SCCs implementation notes) and provide links.
3) Marcus to prepare an Order Form patch that enumerates hosting option selections so procurement can lock SOW obligations.

I'll attach a short CSV-style role matrix in the follow-up. Can you confirm Novasys' preference on telemetry retention and whether they need an explicit data residency SLA?

Best,
Marcus
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass attached

Sara — looping in on the legal side. I reviewed Novasys' v3 redline and the SCCs addendum. Key proposed edits from Redwood Legal (high level):

1) Controller/Processor clarity: We'll accept language that Novasys is the controller and Redwood is the processor for customer content. We will propose explicit language that captures:
   - telemetry as "service operation data" with purpose-limited processing (improvement, debugging, billing).
   - telemetry pseudonymization and 30-day default retention unless customer requests longer.

2) Subprocessor notice & snapshot: We'll commit to providing a subprocessor list snapshot at signature and a 30-day advance notice for changes that materially affect transfer surfaces. We cannot offer unconditional prior approval for every subprocessor (company policy).

3) SCCs flowdown: We'll add a clause ensuring that SCCs are flowed down to subprocessors and that we will provide reasonable evidence of flowdown on request (standardized template).

4) Transfer Addendum: We need to narrow an overly broad carveout in your addendum around "emergency cross-border processing" — propose replacing with a limited list of lawful bases and a requirement to notify within 48 hours.

I attached a short redline excerpt (pdf) and a proposed wording snippet. If Novasys insists on HSM-backed on all production keys for EU data, we will treat that as a deployment-level requirement (Private/Dedicated) and it will impact pricing and lead time.

Proposed timeline to complete DPA + order form patch: 2 weeks if we get confirmation on: (a) telemetry SLA, (b) KMS/HSM requirement (yes/no), (c) whether Novasys needs an explicit export-blocking feature.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sara Mendoza <sara.mendoza@novasys.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novasys.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs — initial pass attached

Laura & Marcus — thank you for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- Telemetry: Novasys can accept 30-day pseudonymized telemetry retention for aggregated metrics. However, we need a guaranteed scrub of any identifiable traces within 7 days for EU-subject data. Is that feasible?

- HSM: We do require HSM-backed key control for any EU regulated personal data. Novasys is open to Private deployment or a Dedicated + BYOK + HSM combo, but procurement needs: (1) pricing delta estimate, (2) expected lead time, and (3) SOC/Audit checklist items we must sign off.

- Transfer addendum: we can accept narrowing the "emergency cross-border processing" clause but want an explicit fallback for DR scenarios where failover might land in a non-EU region. Need a short clause that limits processing to necessary scope and requires notification within 24 hours of failover.

Procurement is copied to flag timelines — if we can get the final DPA and an Order Form patch by Fri 17 Dec, we can keep the December renewal cadence.

Thanks,
Sara

If Novasys can accept the telemetry/DR language and confirm HSM posture by Mon 13 Dec 10:00 AM PT, we should be able to hit 17 Dec signature slot. I'll post the Drive link once the evidence pack is ready.
